items.title: Centralized platform for managing independent dispute resolutions opens - American Hospital Association
items.reason: The opening of a centralized IDR platform directly implements the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution process, which is a core mechanism for resolving balance-billing disputes and a key operational requirement for healthcare revenue-cycle teams.
items.summary: The American Hospital Association announced the launch of a centralized platform for managing independent dispute resolutions (IDR), which is the federal mechanism established under the No Surprises Act for resolving billing disputes between providers and payers. This platform streamlines the IDR process—a key requirement of the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections—allowing healthcare organizations to submit and track dispute resolutions more efficiently. The development directly affects revenue-cycle operations, as hospitals and other providers must use this system to resolve out-of-network billing disputes under federal rules. For revenue-cycle teams, this platform represents a critical tool for managing compliance with the No Surprises Act's IDR procedures and reducing administrative burden in dispute resolution workflows.

items.title: Cigna sued over out-of-network addiction treatment payments - Beinsure
items.reason: This item reports a lawsuit against Cigna, a major health insurer, involving claims-denial or payment disputes related to out-of-network addiction treatment services, which directly falls within the payer litigation and enforcement topic.
items.summary: Cigna has been sued over its payment practices for out-of-network addiction treatment services. The lawsuit addresses disputes regarding how Cigna reimburses for substance-use disorder treatment provided by out-of-network facilities and providers. This case is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it may establish precedent for payer obligations to reimburse out-of-network addiction treatment and could impact claims payment policies and network contracting strategies for behavioral health providers.

items.title: Federal watchdog accuses Humana, UnitedHealthcare Medicare Advantage plans of upcoding
items.reason: This report documents a direct regulatory enforcement action by the HHS OIG against major Medicare Advantage payers (Humana and UnitedHealthcare) for upcoding practices that resulted in substantial overpayments, which is a core payer enforcement matter affecting revenue-cycle operations and reimbursement accuracy.
items.summary: The HHS Office of Inspector General released audits finding that HumanaChoice and UnitedHealthcare of Wisconsin systematically upcoded member health conditions, resulting in approximately $180 million in overpayments over two years. These OIG audits represent a regulatory enforcement action against two of the largest Medicare Advantage insurers for claims-coding violations. The findings directly impact revenue-cycle teams by highlighting payer compliance risks and the potential for audit clawbacks, while signaling increased OIG scrutiny of MA plan coding practices that could affect provider reimbursement and audit exposure across the industry.

items.title: Cigna Beats $3 Million No Surprises Act Lawsuit After Provider Wins Unpaid Awards - Law Commentary
items.reason: This item reports litigation involving a major payer (Cigna) and a lawsuit outcome related to the No Surprises Act, which directly falls within the scope of payer litigation and enforcement affecting revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: Cigna prevailed in a $3 million lawsuit filed under the No Surprises Act, though the provider won unpaid awards as part of the case resolution. The No Surprises Act prohibits surprise billing and imposes requirements on payers regarding out-of-network claims and balance billing protections. This litigation outcome is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because it establishes precedent on how payers must handle No Surprises Act claims and what financial exposure exists for non-compliance. The case illustrates ongoing enforcement activity around surprise billing regulations and the financial stakes involved in payer adherence to federal transparency and payment rules.
